This is an image-space operation dominated by volume resolution and bit-depth [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the operation is 'dominated by volume resolution and bit-depth'. The evidence supports that specific parts of the process (texelization, synthesis, and visualization) are dominated by these factors. However, the evidence explicitly states that the 'rasterization timings depend on mainly the triangle numbers' (scene complexity) and that the overall algorithm's performance is 'insensitive to the scene complexity' only in contrast to other methods, but the rasterization step itself is triangle-dependent. Furthermore, the claim implies the entire operation is dominated by these factors, whereas the evidence breaks down the timing into rasterization (triangle-dependent), texelization/synthesis (resolution/bit-depth dependent), and visualization (resolution dependent). Therefore, while some facts are supported, the generalization that the entire operation is dominated by volume resolution and bit-depth is not fully supported because rasterization depends on triangle count.
